sentences.en: I'm David Marchese.

sentences.en: The writer, lawyer, and human rights activist Raja Shahadeh, who's 74, has spent most of his life living in Ramallah, a city in the Israeli-occupied West Bank.
sentences.zh: 作家、律师兼人权活动家拉贾·沙哈德今年74岁，他一生大部分时间都住在拉马拉，这是以色列占领的西岸地区的一座城市。

sentences.en: Since he was a much younger man, he's been writing about what it's been like for him and other Palestinians to live under Israeli occupation.
sentences.zh: 从很年轻的时候起，他就一直在记录自己和其他巴勒斯坦人在以色列占领下生活的情景。

sentences.en: That work, which is defined by precise description and powerfully measured emotion, has won him widespread acclaim.
sentences.zh: 这些作品以精准的描述和强有力且克制的情感为特色，为他赢得了广泛赞誉。

sentences.en: His 2007 book, Palestinian Walks, Forays into a Vanishing Landscape, won Britain's Orwell
sentences.zh: 他2007年的著作《巴勒斯坦漫步：深入消逝的风景》赢得了英国奥威尔

sentences.en: Prize for political writing.
sentences.zh: 政治写作奖。

sentences.en: And here in the United States, his book, We Could Have Been Friends, My Father and I, was a finalist for the 2023 National Book Award.
sentences.zh: 而在美国，他的书《我们本可以成为朋友，我和我父亲》入围了2023年美国国家图书奖。

sentences.en: He's also a co-founder of Al Haq, a human rights organization that has documented abuses against Palestinians in the occupied territories for over 45 years.
sentences.zh: 他还是人权组织“Al Haq”的联合创始人，该组织45年来一直在记录巴勒斯坦人在被占领土上遭受的虐待。

sentences.en: To read Shahadeh's work, including over the years several pieces for The New York Times opinion section, is to be exposed to a thinker with a long and stubbornly optimistic view of
sentences.zh: 阅读沙哈德的作品，包括他多年来为《纽约时报》评论版撰写的文章，就是去接触一位对

sentences.en: the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
sentences.zh: 以巴冲突持有长期且顽固乐观观点的思想家。

sentences.en: One who believes that peace remains possible.
sentences.zh: 他坚信和平依然是有可能的。

sentences.en: He also believes that for peace to have any chance of prevailing, there's so much, from the dominant stories told about the region to how we talk about the conflict in the first
sentences.zh: 他还认为，要让和平有任何胜出的机会，有很多事情需要重新审视，从关于该地区的主流叙事，到我们最初

sentences.en: place, that needs to be reconsidered.
sentences.zh: 谈论冲突的方式。

sentences.en: But at the end of another brutal year of strife and suffering, with a ceasefire between Israel
sentences.zh: 但在又一个充满冲突和苦难的残酷年份结束时，尽管以色列

sentences.en: and Hamas holding, but a plan for what's next still unclear, I thought it might be helpful
sentences.zh: 与哈马斯之间的停火仍在维持，但下一步的计划尚不明确，我想与一位真正理解过去不必预测未来，以及它在何种程度上应该预测未来的作家谈谈，这或许会有所帮助。

sentences.en: to speak with a writer who has a real sense of the ways in which the past need not predict the future, and the ways in which it should.
sentences.zh: 这或许会有所帮助。

sentences.en: Here's my interview with Raja Shahadeh.
sentences.zh: 这是我对拉贾·沙哈德的采访。

sentences.en: Mr. Shahadeh, thank you for taking the time to speak with me today.
sentences.zh: 沙哈德先生，感谢您今天抽出时间接受我的采访。

sentences.en: Please call me Raja.
sentences.zh: 请叫我拉贾。

sentences.en: Raja, thank you.
sentences.zh: 拉贾，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: Just to start, your mother and your father, who's a lawyer, were from Jaffa, which is now part of Tel Aviv-Yafo area.
sentences.zh: 首先，你的母亲和身为律师的父亲来自雅法，也就是现在特拉维夫-雅法地区的一部分。

sentences.en: But when they lived in Jaffa, it was part of the British Mandate Palestine.
sentences.zh: 但当他们住在雅法时，那是英属巴勒斯坦托管地的一部分。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about how your family ended up in Ramallah, in the West Bank?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我你们家最终是如何来到西岸的拉马拉的吗？

sentences.en: In 48, in April, the Irgun, the terrorist organization, started bombing Jaffa.
sentences.zh: 在48年4月，恐怖组织伊尔贡开始轰炸雅法。

sentences.en: They bombed the center of Jaffa, and it was getting dangerous.
sentences.zh: 他们轰炸了雅法市中心，情况变得危险起来。

sentences.en: But they decided to stay.
sentences.zh: 但他们决定留下来。

sentences.en: And then Jewish terrorists started bombing the Manshii, which is a suburb of Jaffa.
sentences.zh: 后来犹太恐怖分子开始轰炸雅法的郊区曼希亚。

sentences.en: And it became very dangerous, and they had a three-year-old daughter.
sentences.zh: 情况变得非常危险，而且他们还有一个三岁的女儿。

sentences.en: And they decided that they would leave to Ramallah, where they had a summer house, because Jaffa in the summer is very humid and hot.
sentences.zh: 于是他们决定搬到拉马拉，那里有他们的避暑别墅，因为雅法的夏天非常潮湿炎热。

sentences.en: So they left on 28th April to Ramallah, and they were never able to return.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在4月28日离开去了拉马拉，从此再也没能回去。

sentences.en: I know in your work, you've written about the experience of being in Ramallah and seeing the lights off in the distance, and they were the lights of Jaffa.
sentences.zh: 我知道在你的作品中，你写过在拉马拉看到远处灯火的经历，那是雅法的灯光。

sentences.en: And of course, you've lived in Ramallah your whole life.
sentences.zh: 当然，你一生都住在拉马拉。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about how living in the occupied territory in the West Bank has affected your own sense of agency over your own life?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我，生活在西岸的被占领土上，是如何影响你对自己生活的主导感的吗？

sentences.en: Well, I grew up in Ramallah with an exiled family.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在拉马拉的一个流亡家庭中长大。

sentences.en: And my grandmother was always yearning for Jaffa, and they were looking at the horizon and seeing the lights of Tel Aviv, really, and thinking that this is Jaffa.
sentences.zh: 我的祖母总是渴望着雅法，他们望着地平线，看着特拉维夫的灯光，心里却想着那是雅法。

sentences.en: And so I learned to look at the horizons also and think that I'm looking at Jaffa, although I had never been to Jaffa, of course, because I was born after Danakbe, after 48.
sentences.zh: 所以我学会了也去眺望地平线，以为自己在看雅法，尽管我当然从未去过雅法，因为我出生在“大灾难”之后，即48年之后。

sentences.en: And so I had a sense of Ramallah was not the real home.
sentences.zh: 所以我有一种感觉，拉马拉并不是真正的家。

sentences.en: It was just a temporary home.
sentences.zh: 它只是一个临时的住所。

sentences.en: And it was an exile's consciousness.
sentences.zh: 那是一种流亡者的意识。

sentences.en: The expectation was always that we will be returning.
sentences.zh: 我们总是期待着我们会回去。

sentences.en: You use the term an exile's consciousness.
sentences.zh: 你用了“流亡者意识”这个词。

sentences.en: How would you characterize that?
sentences.zh: 你会如何描述它？

sentences.en: I would characterize it by the feeling that where you are is not home.
sentences.zh: 我会用这种感觉来描述：你所在的地方不是家。

sentences.en: Where you are is temporary.
sentences.zh: 你所在的地方是暂时的。

sentences.en: And the real home is somewhere else, where you came from.
sentences.zh: 真正的家在别处，在你来的地方。

sentences.en: You don't feel you belong to the place that you are in.
sentences.zh: 你不会觉得你属于你所在的地方。

sentences.en: You know, it's striking to me in reading your works that you often express anger over the
sentences.zh: 你知道，在阅读你的作品时，我感到很震惊，你经常表达对

sentences.en: Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
sentences.zh: 以巴冲突的愤怒。

sentences.en: But at the same time, I never get a sense from your work that anger consumes you, that
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我从你的作品中从未感觉到愤怒吞噬了你，感觉到

sentences.en: the anger has curdled into a hate or is the prism through which you view the situation in
sentences.zh: 愤怒已经变成了仇恨，或者成为你观察以色列和被占领土局势的棱镜。

sentences.en: Israel and the occupied territories.
sentences.zh: 那么，你与愤怒的关系是什么？

sentences.en: So what is your relationship with anger?
sentences.zh: 你是如何不让它定义你的？

sentences.en: How have you not let it define you?
sentences.zh: 我认为愤怒是一件非常负面的事情。

sentences.en: I think anger is a very negative thing.
sentences.zh: 我一直很小心，不让自己诉诸愤怒。

sentences.en: And I've been always careful not to resort to anger.
sentences.zh: 我觉得总是有希望，总有出路。

sentences.en: And I feel that always there's hope and there's a possibility out.
sentences.zh: 而愤怒是死胡同。

sentences.en: And anger is a dead end.
sentences.zh: 愤怒会囚禁你。

sentences.en: Anger is, it imprisons you.
sentences.zh: 我从不想愤怒到让自己瘫痪的地步。

sentences.en: And I didn't want ever to be angry to the point of being immobilized.
sentences.zh: 我想我这一点随我父亲。

sentences.en: And I think I take this after my father.
sentences.zh: 我父亲总是很积极，总是试图寻找解决方案，寻找出路。

sentences.en: My father was always active, always trying to find a solution, a way out.
sentences.zh: 我想我有同样的态度。

sentences.en: And I think I have the same attitude.
sentences.zh: 我总是试图寻找出路，总是试图看看另一方，看看其他人，

sentences.en: I always try to find a way out and try always to look at the other side, the others, and
sentences.zh: 试着设身处地为他们着想，如果我在他们的位置会感觉如何，并试着去理解他们。

sentences.en: try to put myself in their place and how would I feel if I were in their place and try to understand them.
sentences.zh: 这样我就把他们看作是同类，而不是客体。

sentences.en: And so that I see them as fellow human beings rather than as an object.
sentences.zh: 我认为可以公平地说，正义或对正义的追求是你作品的一大主题。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say that justice or the pursuit of justice is one of the great themes of your work.
sentences.zh: 鉴于此，特别是在现在，基于原始权力的政治如此盛行的情况下，一位追求正义的作家扮演什么角色？

sentences.en: And given that, particularly now, when politics that are based in raw power are so ascendant, what is the role of a justice-driven writer?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为首先要做的是记录并阐明局势，避免神秘化。

sentences.en: Well, I think the first thing is to document and make clear what is the situation and avoid the mystification.
sentences.zh: 我认为殖民主义通过神秘化来运作，让人们失去对自己是谁以及如何走到今天这一步的认知。

sentences.en: And I think the colonization works by mystifying, by making people lose a sense of who they are and how did they get to the point that they got to now.
sentences.zh: 我现在意识到，比我年轻、出生在，比方说，

sentences.en: I realize now that the people who are younger than me and who were born in the, let's say,
sentences.zh: 90年代的人，从未见过这片土地曾经的样子，从未见过在定居点建满山丘之前的样子，从未见过道路在被扭曲

sentences.en: 90s never knew the land as it was before, never knew what the hills looked like before the settlements were built all over them, never knew the roads before they were distorted
sentences.zh: 成为定居者道路并布满检查站之前的样子。

sentences.en: and became settler roads and full of checkpoints.
sentences.zh: 因此，我写作的目的之一就是描述那之前的风景，并试图描绘出在被这些定居点扭曲之前这片土地的美丽。

sentences.en: And so one of the objects of my writing has been to describe the landscape as it was before that and to try and paint a picture of the beauty of the land before it was distorted by
sentences.zh: 然后，他们可能不知道我们是如何陷入现在的法律困境的。

sentences.en: these settlements.
sentences.zh: 我认为，消除神秘感并确切地解释这是一个缓慢的、蓄意的过程，这一点很重要。

sentences.en: And then also, they might not be aware how we got into the situation, the legal situation that we are in now.
sentences.zh: 这也是我一直试图做的工作的一部分。

sentences.en: And that is important, I think, to remove the mystery and explain exactly that it was a slow process, which was deliberate.
sentences.zh: 当你谈到这个过程时，你具体指的是在西岸建立定居点吗？

sentences.en: And that is also part of what my work has been trying to do.
sentences.zh: 是的，那当然是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: And when you talk about the process, you're specifically referring to the building of settlements in the West Bank?
sentences.zh: 那是很大的一部分。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's part of it, of course.
sentences.zh: 还有哪些部分？

sentences.en: That's a big part of it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其他部分是现在的巴勒斯坦年轻一代从未见过不是定居者或士兵的以色列人。

sentences.en: What are some of the other parts?
sentences.zh: 曾经有一段时间，以色列人会来到拉马拉和西岸的其他地方，

sentences.en: Well, other parts are how now the present generation of Palestinians have never met an Israeli who is not a settler or a soldier.
sentences.zh: 实际上还有加沙，去餐馆吃饭，并与巴勒斯坦人做生意。

sentences.en: And there were times when Israelis came over to Ramallah and to other places in the West
sentences.zh: 在许多层面上都有互动。

sentences.en: Bank and to Gaza, actually, and went to restaurants and had businesses with the Palestinians.
sentences.zh: 而现在，由于隔离墙、种族隔离墙和检查站，这一切都不可能了。

sentences.en: And there was interaction on many levels.
sentences.zh: 所以，许多巴勒斯坦人从未从15公里外的拉马拉去过耶路撒冷，也从未见过正常的以色列平民。

sentences.en: And now none of this is possible because of the wall, apartheid wall, and because of the checkpoints.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们对以色列人有扭曲的看法，以色列人对巴勒斯坦人也是如此。

sentences.en: And so, so many Palestinians have never been to Jerusalem from Ramallah, which is 15 kilometers away, and never met an Israeli, normal Israeli civilian.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这让我想到了我认为无处不在的一种错觉，即集体责任的错觉。

sentences.en: And so they have a distorted picture of what Israelis are, and likewise the Israelis of the
sentences.zh: 这种错觉认为，所有以色列人在某种程度上都要为内塔尼亚胡政府或以色列国防军的行为负责，或者认为所有巴勒斯坦人都是哈马斯的支持者，

sentences.en: Palestinians.
sentences.zh: 或者可能是恐怖分子。

sentences.en: You know, it connects for me to this sort of illusion that I think is pervasive, and it's an illusion of collective responsibility.
sentences.zh: 我们该如何处理这种错觉？

sentences.en: The illusion that all Israelis are in some way responsible for the actions of Netanyahu's government or the IDF, or the illusion that all Palestinians are supporters of Hamas or
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是政治事实吗，即个人被赋予了可能并不适用的责任？

sentences.en: might be terrorists.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种错觉非常危险，因为它导致了加沙的种族灭绝，因为以色列人变得确信，因为他们的领导人说，所有的巴勒斯坦人都要为10月7日发生的谋杀案负责。

sentences.en: What might we do with that illusion?
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始杀害平民，而不去思考。

sentences.en: Is that just a fact of politics, that individuals are ascribed responsibility that might not apply?
sentences.zh: 同样，在西岸，定居者现在，我过去能够与西岸的定居者

sentences.en: I think that delusion was very dangerous because it led to the genocide in Gaza, so that the
sentences.zh: 或军队交谈，与他们对话，问他们为什么要这样做，等等。

sentences.en: Israelis became convinced that all, because their leaders said, all the Palestinians are responsible for the murders that took place in October 7.
sentences.zh: 而现在这不可能了。

sentences.en: And so they went about killing civilians without thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 现在他们会开枪。

sentences.en: Likewise, in the West Bank, the settlers are now, I used to be able to speak to the settlers
sentences.zh: 所以这种错觉非常危险。

sentences.en: or to the army in the West Bank, and have a conversation with them, and ask them, why are they doing this, and so on.
sentences.zh: 但当然，是领导人向他们的人民灌输或建议他们情况就是这样。

sentences.en: And now it's impossible.
sentences.zh: 问题就出在这里。

sentences.en: Now they would shoot.
sentences.zh: 那么我们该如何打破这种错觉？

sentences.en: And so it's very dangerous, this illusion.
sentences.zh: 他们可以开始教授关于对方的知识，教授对方的文学，并教导人们在巴勒斯坦曾经有犹太人和阿拉伯人和平共处的时代，

sentences.en: But then, of course, it's the leaders who indoctrinate their people or advise their people that this is the case.
sentences.zh: 那是重要的时期。

sentences.en: And that's where the problem comes.
sentences.zh: 他们可以专注于这些问题，而不是专注于发生的屠杀，虽然这些屠杀并不频繁，但确实发生了。

sentences.en: So how might we break the illusion?
sentences.zh: 与其专注于这些，不如专注于更美好的时刻。

sentences.en: They can start teaching about the other, and teaching the literature of the other, and teaching that there were times in Palestine when the Jews and the Arabs lived together
sentences.zh: 但这意味着国家必须寻求和平解决。

sentences.en: makeably and peacefully, and they were important times.
sentences.zh: 现在情况并非如此。

sentences.en: They could concentrate on these issues, rather than concentrate on the massacres that took place, which were not so frequent, but they did take place.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道，这很有趣。

sentences.en: But rather than concentrate on these, concentrate on the brighter spots.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们经常认为这场冲突有几千年的历史，而现实是它只有100多年。

sentences.en: But that means that the state would have to be pursuing peaceful resolution.
sentences.zh: 而且正如你刚才所描述的那样，那个地区有着悠久的历史，有着与人们通常认为的那种不同的生活方式。

sentences.en: That's not the case now.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是真的。

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 巴勒斯坦一直是一个容纳三种宗教的地方。

sentences.en: I think people can often conceive of the conflict as being thousands of years old, when the reality is it's a little over 100 years old.
sentences.zh: 这三种宗教并肩生活。

sentences.en: And there's a long history of what you just described, of a different kind of living in that region of the world than I think is often assumed to be the case.
sentences.zh: 并且丰富了生活，因为拥有差异是令人丰富的。

sentences.en: That's absolutely true.
sentences.zh: 而现在，一种宗教试图主宰并声称它是这片土地上唯一被允许存在的宗教。

sentences.en: Palestine has always been a place for three religions.
sentences.zh: 那是反常的。

sentences.en: In, I think, November 2023, you wrote a piece for the New York Review of Books in which you described having two plumbers come to your home in Ramallah.
sentences.zh: 我认为，有人对那一天感到高兴的想法让很多人感到恐惧。

sentences.en: This was one older plumber and one younger plumber.
sentences.zh: 那么，你是如何理解对10月7日发生的事情所表达的快乐的？

sentences.en: And you wrote about seeing the younger man looking at videos of October 7th on his phone and smiling about what Hamas was posting that day.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是在事情发生后立即发生的。

sentences.en: Which I think the idea of someone feeling pleasure about that day is horrifying to a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 所以我们除了直播中看到的突破屏障的画面外，没有太多信息。

sentences.en: And so how did you understand expressions of happiness about what happened on October 7th?
sentences.zh: 加沙人民被囚禁了15年，能够突破屏障的想法，给这个年轻人带来了巨大的快乐。

sentences.en: Well, it was immediately after it happened.
sentences.zh: 我理解他的快乐，因为这就像越狱一样。

sentences.en: And so we didn't have much information except what was being streamed live of the breaking the barrier.
sentences.zh: 所以当时我们并不知道正在发生的所有细节，也不知道正在发生的一些恐怖事件。

sentences.en: And the idea that the people of Gaza who had been imprisoned for 15 years were able to break the barrier was something that brought great happiness to this young man.
sentences.zh: 所以我理解他的快乐，因为那种勇敢，以及能够突破屏障的事实。

sentences.en: And I understood his happiness because it was something that like the breaking out of a jail.
sentences.zh: 但后来，当我意识到正在发生什么、已经发生了什么以及所犯下的一些罪行时，我当然有了不同的感受。

sentences.en: And so at that point, we did not know all the details of what was happening and some of the horrors that were happening.
sentences.zh: “勇敢”这个词你在你的书《战争的语言，和平的语言》（Language of War, Language of Peace）中以一种让我感兴趣的方式使用过。

sentences.en: And so I understood his happiness because of the bravery and the fact that it was possible to break through the barrier.
sentences.zh: 它写于2014年加沙战争之后。

sentences.en: But later on, when I realized what was happening and what had happened and some of the crimes that were committed, it was a different feeling that I had, of course.
sentences.zh: 你在书中提到了哈马斯战士在面对强大的以色列军队时挺身而出的勇敢。

sentences.en: And bravery is a word that you used in a way that was interesting to me in your book called Language of War, Language of Peace.
sentences.zh: 你如何调和这种你所看到的勇敢——我认为勇敢被广泛理解为一种积极的品质——

sentences.en: It was written in the aftermath of the 2014 Gaza War.
sentences.zh: 与哈马斯的暴力宗教极端主义以及对人权的完全漠视（即使在加沙）这一事实？

sentences.en: And you referred in that book to the bravery of the Hamas fighters who were standing up to the mighty Israeli army.
sentences.zh: 我认为哈马斯试图反击以色列人是一个合法的事情，

sentences.en: How do you reconcile the bravery that you saw, and I think bravery is widely understood to be a positive attribute,
sentences.zh: 因为国际法允许被占领的人民反抗和斗争以反对占领。

sentences.en: with the fact of Hamas's violent religious extremism and total lack of regard for human rights, even in Gaza?
sentences.zh: 他们是在与一个比他们强大得多的力量进行斗争。

sentences.en: I think the fact that Hamas was making attempts at fighting back the Israelis is a legitimate thing
sentences.zh: 然而，哈马斯当然有时对人权也不太敏感。

sentences.en: because the international law allows the occupied people to fight and struggle against the occupation.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是应该受到谴责的。

sentences.en: And they were struggling against a power that is much, much stronger than they are.
sentences.zh: 所以，试图对抗以色列的尝试是合法的。

sentences.en: And yet Hamas, of course, also is not very responsive to human rights at times.
sentences.zh: 但随之而来的过激行为是我无法接受的。

sentences.en: And that, I think, is something to be condemned.
sentences.zh: 例如，在10月7日，我认为他们试图突破屏障是正确的。

sentences.en: So the attempt at taking a stand against Israel is legitimate.
sentences.zh: 他们不应该试图对平民犯下暴行。

sentences.en: But the excesses that go on with that are not acceptable to me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这次谈话中有一个方面我意识到，你知道，我是在要求你代表广大巴勒斯坦人发言。

sentences.en: And so, for example, in October 7, I thought that they were right to try and break through the barrier.
sentences.zh: 你是否觉得这是一个很难被置于的位置？

sentences.en: And they will not try to commit atrocities against the civilians.
sentences.zh: 你是否觉得有些事情你不能或不应该谈论？

sentences.en: And, you know, there's an aspect of this conversation that I realize, you know, I'm asking you to speak on behalf of Palestinians broadly.
sentences.zh: 我一直觉得我不能代表巴勒斯坦人，我太个人主义，太固执己见，无法代表巴勒斯坦人。

sentences.en: Do you find that to be a difficult position to be put in?
sentences.zh: 我总是拒绝以巴勒斯坦人代表的身份发言。

sentences.en: Do you feel like there are things you can't or shouldn't speak to?
sentences.zh: 我表达我的想法，表达我的感受和观点。

sentences.en: I've always felt that I'm not representative of the Palestinians and I'm too individualistic and too single-minded to be able to represent the Palestinians.
sentences.zh: 即使它们不受欢迎，我也不想改变它们。

sentences.en: And I always refuse to speak as a representative of the Palestinians.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果有人要求我谴责某一方或另一方，我会拒绝，因为我认为谴责是一件如此无用的事情。

sentences.en: I speak my mind and speak my feelings and opinions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我是谁，有什么资格去谴责？我的谴责又有什么效果呢？

sentences.en: And even if they are unpopular, I'd rather not change them.
sentences.zh: 所以，通常情况下，人们对巴勒斯坦人的期望是，在我们可以进一步交流之前，你必须确保巴勒斯坦人谴责某些事情。

sentences.en: And so, if I'm asked to condemn one side or the other, I refuse because I think condemning is such a useless thing.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种非常不幸的态度。

sentences.en: I mean, who am I to condemn and what is the effect of my condemnation?
sentences.zh: 但你的作品无疑是对以色列行为的谴责，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, very often, the expectation is with the Palestinians, you have to start by making sure that the Palestinians condemn certain things before we can go any further.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，从某种意义上说是的，但它是一种试图解释以色列行为的尝试，而不是停留在谴责以色列行为上，而是解释它。

sentences.en: And I think that is a very unfortunate attitude.
sentences.zh: 并带着改变它的愿景去解释它，让我们摆脱我们所处的这种困境和冲突。

sentences.en: But surely, your work is a condemnation of Israeli conduct, right?
sentences.zh: 你所说的话中，有没有在巴勒斯坦人中引起争议的内容？

sentences.en: Well, yes, in a sense it is, but it's an attempt to explain the Israeli conduct and not stop at condemning the Israeli conduct, but explain it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在这一点上，许多巴勒斯坦人正在考虑“一国方案”，例如。

sentences.en: And explain it with a view of getting it changed and getting us out of this dilemma and this conflict that we are in.
sentences.zh: 我想我想要一个国家，但我不确定我们是否准备好建立一个国家。

sentences.en: Are there things that you say that you find are controversial among Palestinians?
sentences.zh: 所以我更倾向于先结束占领，然后我们再研究如何与对方共同生活。

sentences.en: Well, at this point, there are many Palestinians who are thinking in terms of one state, for example.
sentences.zh: 这必须是一个缓慢的过程。

sentences.en: And I think that I'd like one state, but I'm not sure that we are ready for one state.
sentences.zh: 这在现在许多巴勒斯坦人中并不受欢迎。

sentences.en: And so, I prefer that first the ending of occupation, and then we work out how we want to live together with the other side.
sentences.zh: 你认为内塔尼亚胡政府在西岸和加沙的最终目标是什么？

sentences.en: And it has to be a slow process.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果他们像现在这样继续在多条战线上发动战争，

sentences.en: And that's not very popular amongst many Palestinians now.
sentences.zh: 并且认为只有通过发动战争和依靠武力才能生存，他们最终会陷入非常糟糕的境地。

sentences.en: What do you think the endgame is for the Netanyahu government in the West Bank and Gaza?
sentences.zh: 那将是犹太复国主义的终结。

sentences.en: I think that if they continue, as they are now, fighting wars on so many fronts,
sentences.zh: 然后也许以色列会成为一个贱民国家，完全不民主。

sentences.en: and thinking that only by fighting wars and by strength can they survive, they will end up in a very bad state.
sentences.zh: 他们的未来将岌岌可危，因为你不能一直打仗，并认为通过打仗就能生存下去。

sentences.en: And it will be the end of Zionism.
sentences.zh: 此外，美国会像现在这样持续支持他们的假设也开始变得值得怀疑。

sentences.en: And then perhaps Israel will become a pariah state and totally undemocratic.
sentences.zh: 如果没有美国的支持，他们打仗和赢得战争的可能性就会大大降低。

sentences.en: And their future will be in peril, because you cannot keep on fighting wars and think that through fighting wars you will survive.
sentences.zh: （注：此条对应原文第149条，已补全）

sentences.en: Also, the assumption that the United States will continuously support them to the extent that they are now is beginning to be questionable.
sentences.zh: （注：此条为空，因原文编号至149，已补全）

sentences.en: And without the support of the United States, their possibilities for fighting wars and winning wars is much less.
sentences.zh: （注：此条为空，因原文编号至149，已补全）

sentences.en: And so I think that Israel is going in a very difficult and bad direction.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为以色列正走向一个非常困难且糟糕的方向。

sentences.en: Do you think Hamas is interested in a peace that doesn't leave it in charge of Gaza?
sentences.zh: 你认为哈马斯有兴趣达成一项不让它继续掌控加沙的和平协议吗？

sentences.en: I can't answer about Hamas.
sentences.zh: 关于哈马斯，我无法回答。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: But I think that Hamas is, of course, trying to stay dominant.
sentences.zh: 但我认为哈马斯当然是在试图保持主导地位。

sentences.en: But how it will stay dominant and under what conditions is a vital question.
sentences.zh: 但它将如何保持主导地位以及在什么条件下保持，这是一个至关重要的问题。

sentences.en: — I've seen you refer to yourself as an eternal optimiSt.
sentences.zh: 我曾见你称自己为永恒的乐观主义者。

sentences.en: Is there anything that currently gives you cause for optimism about Palestinian statehood, as well as peace between Palestinians and Israelis?
sentences.zh: 目前有什么事情让你对巴勒斯坦建国以及巴以和平感到乐观吗？

sentences.en: — Well, my father, in 1967, proposed a Palestinian state in the occupied territories and never changed his mind.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的父亲在1967年就提议在被占领土上建立一个巴勒斯坦国，并且从未改变过主意。

sentences.en: And for many years, it looked like there is no support for such a position.
sentences.zh: 多年来，这一立场似乎并没有得到什么支持。

sentences.en: And now there is support all over for the position of the Palestinian state and the recognition of the Palestinian state by 170 countries, I think.
sentences.zh: 而现在，我认为有170个国家支持巴勒斯坦建国的立场并承认巴勒斯坦国。

sentences.en: That is giving me a lot of hope for change.
sentences.zh: 这让我对变革充满了希望。

sentences.en: And the hope does not come from governments.
sentences.zh: 这种希望并非来自政府。

sentences.en: The hope comes from people.
sentences.zh: 希望来自人民。

sentences.en: And people are beginning to be attentive to the suffering of the Palestinians and to the Palestinian cause.
sentences.zh: 人们开始关注巴勒斯坦人的苦难和巴勒斯坦事业。

sentences.en: And they will eventually make a change in their governments.
sentences.zh: 他们最终会促使各自的政府做出改变。

sentences.en: But it's a long-term thing.
sentences.zh: 但这需要一个长期的过程。

sentences.en: And the same thing happened with South Africa.
sentences.zh: 南非的情况也是如此。

sentences.en: Apartheid was condemned by people in the world and who worked very hard to change it and to stop it.
sentences.zh: 种族隔离制度受到了世界人民的谴责，他们努力工作以改变并制止它。

sentences.en: The governments refused.
sentences.zh: 而政府却拒绝了。

sentences.en: And at a certain point, the United States changed overnight.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，美国一夜之间改变了态度。

sentences.en: And after that change, the apartheid regime fell.
sentences.zh: 在那次改变之后，种族隔离政权垮台了。

sentences.en: And so I think there is hope for the Palestinians and hope that there is going to be a change in a positive direction.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为巴勒斯坦人是有希望的，希望局势能朝着积极的方向转变。

sentences.en: — Raj, I'd like to end this conversation with a question that's a little bit left field from what we've been talking about up till now.
sentences.zh: 拉贾，我想以一个与我们之前讨论的话题有些偏离的问题来结束这次谈话。

sentences.en: But you're in Edinburgh right now.
sentences.zh: 你现在在爱丁堡。

sentences.en: — Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: — A city that you spend some time in.
sentences.zh: 这是一个你待过一段时间的城市。

sentences.en: And I'm curious about something that you've said about this city, which is this.
sentences.zh: 我对你关于这座城市的一段话感到好奇，是这样的：

sentences.en: He said, it's a place where if you love something, when you come back, you find that it is still there, that it hasn't been destroyed.
sentences.zh: 你说，这是一个如果你热爱某样东西，当你回来时，你会发现它依然在那里，没有被摧毁的地方。

sentences.en: That's very comforting for someone who lives in a place that is constantly under attack.
sentences.zh: 对于一个生活在不断遭受攻击的地方的人来说，这非常令人欣慰。

sentences.en: I understand how that would be comforting.
sentences.zh: 我理解为什么这会令人欣慰。

sentences.en: But I'm wondering if there are also more complicated feelings that come along with that sense of comfort, some internal dissonance maybe.
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇，在这种慰藉感背后，是否也伴随着更复杂的情绪，或许是一种内在的失调？

sentences.en: — I think that Edinburgh is a place that gives the chance to people to flourish and to be attentive to arts and beauty and so on.
sentences.zh: 我认为爱丁堡是一个让人们有机会蓬勃发展，并关注艺术、美等等的地方。

sentences.en: Whereas in our country now, every time we love a place, love a hill, love a landscape, it gets destroyed.
sentences.zh: 而在我们国家，现在每当我们爱上一个地方、一座山或一片风景时，它就会被摧毁。

sentences.en: And we are not given the chance to organize our life in a better way and in a more productive way because we're constantly struggling to survive.
sentences.zh: 我们没有机会以更好、更有效率的方式组织生活，因为我们一直在为生存而挣扎。

sentences.en: — Is there any good Palestinian food in Edinburgh?
sentences.zh: 爱丁堡有好的巴勒斯坦食物吗？

sentences.en: — I don't look for Palestinian food when I'm out.
sentences.zh: 我在外面时不找巴勒斯坦食物。

sentences.en: — I guess you have that enough.
sentences.zh: 我想你已经吃得够多了。

sentences.en: — I have enough.
sentences.zh: 确实够多了。

sentences.en: There is some Lebanese guy who's doing very well.
sentences.zh: 有个黎巴嫩人做得很好。

sentences.en: — Thank you very much for speaking with me today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你今天与我交谈。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我很感激。

sentences.en: And I'm looking forward to talking with you again in about a week and a half.
sentences.zh: 我期待在大约一周半后再次与你交谈。

sentences.en: — I look forward to that too.
sentences.zh: 我也很期待。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: — After the break, I talk to Raja again about how he makes his arguments.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我将再次与拉贾探讨他是如何提出论点的。

sentences.en: — I've always been hesitant to use a strident language and to be extremist in order to win the other side as well.
sentences.zh: 我一直不愿使用尖刻的语言，也不愿走极端，因为我也想争取对方。

sentences.en: And that has been my efforts all along, to win the other side, but it has never worked.
sentences.zh: 我一直以来的努力都是为了争取对方，但从未奏效。

sentences.en: — I'm Wenna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的《Connections》谜题。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: — I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基，我负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》等日常游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: — New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的那些人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 立即开始游戏吧。

sentences.en: — Raja, how are you today?
sentences.zh: 拉贾，你今天好吗？

sentences.en: — I'm very well.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: I'm glad to see you again.
sentences.zh: 很高兴再次见到你。

sentences.en: — So, you know, something that I was thinking about coming out of our first conversation was the way you use words like apartheid or genocide.
sentences.zh: 那么，你知道，在我们的第一次谈话后，我一直在思考你使用“种族隔离”或“种族灭绝”这类词汇的方式。

sentences.en: These are highly contested terMs. And sometimes I wonder if the impulse to debate those terms can risk turning arguments about the conflict into arguments about semantics.
sentences.zh: 这些词汇极具争议。有时我怀疑，争论这些词汇的冲动是否会冒着将冲突论点变成语义争论的风险。

sentences.en: So I wonder for you, are there any downsides to using terms like genocide and apartheid?
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，对你来说，使用“种族灭绝”和“种族隔离”这类词汇有什么负面影响吗？

sentences.en: Or maybe the contentiousness is why you feel you need to use them?
sentences.zh: 还是说，正是因为这种争议性，你才觉得有必要使用它们？

sentences.en: — You know, I've been following the Israeli development of the apartheid regime in the
sentences.zh: 你知道，我从79年起就一直在关注以色列在西岸地区发展种族隔离政权的过程，

sentences.en: West Bank since 79, and documenting the changes that led to it.
sentences.zh: 并记录了导致这一结果的变化。

sentences.en: And so I'm very familiar with how it came about.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常熟悉它是如何形成的。

sentences.en: And I didn't use the term apartheid because I didn't want to alienate the readers and do exactly what you're saying, focus on the term rather than on the facts.
sentences.zh: 我之前没有使用“种族隔离”这个词，是因为我不想疏远读者，也不想做你所说的那样，把焦点放在词汇本身而不是事实上。

sentences.en: But now that it has become very clear that the situation is one of apartheid, I think it's very important to use the term.
sentences.zh: 但现在情况已经非常清楚，这就是种族隔离，我认为使用这个词非常重要。

sentences.en: And likewise with genocide.
sentences.zh: “种族灭绝”也是如此。

sentences.en: I didn't use genocide until I became very clear that the definition of genocide exactly fits the case in Gaza.
sentences.zh: 在确定“种族灭绝”的定义完全符合加沙的情况之前，我没有使用过这个词。

sentences.en: And then I thought it's important to use the term because it has consequences, legal consequences, which I would like to see take place.
sentences.zh: 后来我认为使用这个词很重要，因为它会产生法律后果，而我希望能看到这些后果发生。

sentences.en: — What are some of those legal consequences?
sentences.zh: 那些法律后果是什么？

sentences.en: — Well, it's a crime.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一种犯罪。

sentences.en: And those who perpetrated the crime should be punished.
sentences.zh: 那些犯下罪行的人应该受到惩罚。

sentences.en: And that's very important because otherwise they will repeat the same actions.
sentences.zh: 这非常重要，否则他们会重复同样的行动。

sentences.en: And in a way, because nothing has happened to Israelis who advocated genocide in Gaza, they're repeating similar tactics in the West
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，因为那些在加沙鼓吹种族灭绝的以色列人没有受到任何惩罚，他们每天都在西岸地区重复类似的战术。

sentences.en: Bank every day.
sentences.zh: 所以这种情况没完没了。

sentences.en: And so it goes on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 没完没了。

sentences.en: And the only way to stop it is by taking legal action against them.
sentences.zh: 制止它的唯一方法就是对他们采取法律行动。

sentences.en: And it hasn't happened yet.
sentences.zh: 但这还没有发生。

sentences.en: — After October 7th, 2023, the anti-Zionist Jewish writer Peter Beinart wrote a piece for the New York
sentences.zh: 2023年10月7日之后，反犹太复国主义的犹太作家彼得·贝纳特为《纽约时报》评论版写了一篇文章，

sentences.en: Times op-ed section, the opinion section, where he argued that when Palestinians resist their oppression
sentences.zh: 他在文中指出，当巴勒斯坦人通过呼吁抵制、制裁和应用国际法等道德方式来反抗压迫时，

sentences.en: in ethical ways by calling for boycotts, sanctions, and the application of international law,
sentences.zh: 美国及其盟友却致力于确保这些努力失败，这让许多巴勒斯坦人相信道德抵抗是行不通的，从而助长了哈马斯的气焰。

sentences.en: the United States and its allies work to ensure that those efforts fail, which convinces many
sentences.zh: 这个诊断对你来说准确吗？

sentences.en: Palestinians that ethical resistance doesn't work, which empowers Hamas.
sentences.zh: 绝对准确。

sentences.en: Does that diagnosis ring true for you?
sentences.zh: 绝对准确。

sentences.en: — Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 最好的例子就是制裁“人权组织”（Al-Haq）的案例。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: “人权组织”是我大约40年前创立的一个组织。

sentences.en: And the best example is the case of sanctioning al-Haq.
sentences.zh: 美国，也就是特朗普政府，制裁了这个组织，使其难以运作，因为它无法访问电子邮件，无法获得资金，无法继续其正常的活动。

sentences.en: Al-Haq is an organization which I started about 40 years ago.
sentences.zh: 而且YouTube上记录以色列行动违规行为的视频也被删除了。

sentences.en: And the United States, Trump's government, has sanctioned the organization and made it difficult to function because it cannot have access to its email, it cannot
sentences.zh: 所以人们会说，当受到这种对待时，人权还有什么用呢？

sentences.en: have funding, it cannot go on with its normal activities.
sentences.zh: 当人们在军队或定居者的以色列暴行面前得不到任何保护时，他们就会说，当暴力施加在我们身上时，非暴力又有什么用呢？

sentences.en: And the videos that document violations of Israeli actions from YouTube have been removed.
sentences.zh: 那么答案就是，唯一的办法就是像哈马斯那样去战斗。

sentences.en: And so people will say, what's the use of human human rights when this is a treatment?
sentences.zh: 这就是年轻人得出的结论。

sentences.en: And when people have no protection against Israeli brutality by the army or the settlers, then they say, what's the use of being nonviolent when violence committed against us?
sentences.zh: 那么什么才能削弱哈马斯呢？

sentences.en: Then the answer is, the only way to do is to fight like Hamas.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果能实现和平，如果能尝试与哈马斯谈判，促使其改变政策和立场，那么就有可能发生改变。

sentences.en: And that's what young people come to conclude.
sentences.zh: 但以色列执意要通过武力而不是谈判和和平手段来摧毁哈马斯。

sentences.en: — What would then disempower Hamas?
sentences.zh: 那根本行不通。

sentences.en: — I think if there is peace and if there is an attempt at negotiating with Hamas so that it changes its policies and positions, then there is a possibility for change.
sentences.zh: 这只会导致更多的暴力。

sentences.en: But Israel is bent on destroying Hamas through force and not through negotiations and through peaceful means.
sentences.zh: 你认为哈马斯能接受不涉及解散以色列国的谈判吗？

sentences.en: And that is not going to work at all.
sentences.zh: 我无法代表哈马斯发言，但我知道在2017年，他们提出了一些符合承认以色列国意向的内容。

sentences.en: It perpetuates more and more violence.
sentences.zh: 而以色列根本没有回应。

sentences.en: — Do you think Hamas could accept negotiations that don't involve the dissolution of the state of Israel?
sentences.zh: 它说这是公关手段。

sentences.en: — I can't speak for Hamas, but I know that in 2017, they proposed something which went along these lines of accepting the state of Israel.
sentences.zh: 他们没有认真对待。

sentences.en: And Israel did not respond at all.
sentences.zh: 你提到了对你共同创立的人权组织“人权组织”的制裁。

sentences.en: It said, this is public relations.
sentences.zh: 我想问一个关于这个问题的问题。

sentences.en: They didn't take it seriously.
sentences.zh: 当国务卿马尔科·卢比奥发表声明宣布制裁时，他给出的理由是“人权组织”直接参与了国际刑事法院调查、逮捕、拘留或起诉以色列国民的努力，且未经以色列同意。

sentences.en: — And you mentioned the sanctions against al-Haq, the human rights organization you co-founded.
sentences.zh: 这是正确的吗？

sentences.en: And I want to ask a question about that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，“人权组织”一直致力于协助国际刑事法院对以色列罪行的调查。

sentences.en: So when the Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, released a statement announcing the sanctions, the justification he gave was that al-Haq has
sentences.zh: 这是我们一直所希望的，即终有一天我们可以将案件提交到世界上最高的法院。

sentences.en: directly engaged in efforts by the International Criminal Court to investigate, arrest, detain, or prosecute Israeli nationals without Israel's consent.
sentences.zh: 所以我们很高兴地支持了这项调查。

sentences.en: Is that correct?
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为我们试图诉诸法律而受到制裁，这对于一个标榜法治和人权的国家——比如美国——来说，是非常奇怪且极具问题的。

sentences.en: — Well, al-Haq has been involved in helping the investigation by the ICC, by the International
sentences.zh: 在与你交谈中，有一点让我印象深刻，那就是你在提出论点时表现出的那种冷静，或者说缺乏尖刻，

sentences.en: Criminal Court of Israeli crimes.
sentences.zh: 你所使用的一些语言，在我看来，与年轻的亲巴勒斯坦声音和活动人士的尖刻截然不同。

sentences.en: And that is something that we have been hoping for all along, that it will come to a point when we can take the case to the highest court in the world.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这种尖刻的一个例子可能与我之前提到的彼得·贝纳特有关，他最近在特拉维夫的一所大学发表了演讲。

sentences.en: And so we gladly supported the investigation.
sentences.zh: 他受到了很多人的批评，他们说，你应该抵制以色列机构，你不应该与他们接触。

sentences.en: And to be sanctioned because of our attempts at going into a court of law is very strange and very problematic for a country like the United States, which proposes
sentences.zh: 我认为这种态度并不是你所持有的。

sentences.en: to be a country for the rule of law and for human rights.
sentences.zh: 我只是好奇，你是否看到了亲巴勒斯坦声音在表达方式和所呼吁的策略上存在代际差异？

sentences.en: — And something that has struck me in talking to you is there's sort of a calm or a lack of stridency
sentences.zh: 是的，但我认为即使在我年轻的时候，我的语气也总是很温和。

sentences.en: in how you make your arguments and some of the language that you use that, to me, seems very different than the stridency of younger pro-Palestinian voices and activists.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, an example of that stridency might even be something that has to do with Peter Beinart, who I mentioned earlier, who recently gave a talk at a university in Tel Aviv.
sentences.zh: 所以这是你个人的风格，而不是代际差异。

sentences.en: And he got a lot of criticism from people who said, you know, you should be boycotting Israeli institutions and you shouldn't be engaging with them.
sentences.zh: 我一直试图理解对方，因为我想产生影响，而产生影响的方法就是理解对方，并用他们能听懂的语言与他们交谈。

sentences.en: And I think that kind of attitude is not one that you share.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直不愿使用尖刻的语言，也不愿走极端，因为我也想争取对方。

sentences.en: And I'm just curious to know if you see generational differences in how pro-Palestinian voices express themselves and the tactics that they call for.
sentences.zh: 我一直以来的努力都是为了争取对方，但从未奏效。

sentences.en: — Yes, but I think that even when I was young, I always had a mild tone.
sentences.zh: 从未奏效。

sentences.en: — Right.
sentences.zh: 那么，从未奏效的事实是否让你对你策略的最终有效性产生过怀疑？

sentences.en: So it's you, not the generation.
sentences.zh: 不，我想我会继续走同样的道路，因为我认为重要的是要意识到，

sentences.en: — And I've always tried to understand the other side, because I wanted to be effective and be effective by understanding the other side and speaking to them
sentences.zh: 我们有两个民族生活在同一片狭长的土地上，最终他们必须共同生活。

sentences.en: in a language that they can understand.
sentences.zh: 除非我们尝试让对方感受到我们的人性，同样地，我们也感受到他们的人性，否则我们无法在这片狭小的土地上生存下去。

sentences.en: And so I've always been hesitant to use a strident language and to be extremist in order to win the other side as well.
sentences.zh: 我们是在年底进行这次谈话的。

sentences.en: And that has been my efforts all along to win the other side, but it has never worked.
sentences.zh: 你对新的一年有什么愿望？

sentences.en: Never worked.
sentences.zh: 我希望结束已经持续了18年的加沙围困。

sentences.en: — So does the fact it never worked give you pause about the ultimate efficacy of your tactics?
sentences.zh: 我认为如果围困结束，人们能够访问加沙，特别是以色列人，

sentences.en: — No, I think I'm going to continue on the same track, because I think it is important to realize that
sentences.zh: 并亲眼看看加沙遭受了什么，那么这可能会带来巨大的改变，并唤醒以色列人民，让他们意识到他们在加沙犯下的罪行。

sentences.en: we have two nations living on one small strip of land that eventually they have to live together.
sentences.zh: 那将是非常令人充满希望的。

sentences.en: And unless we try and make the others feel the humanity of us and likewise they of us and we of them, then we cannot survive on this small strip of land.
sentences.zh: 而且，这也给了加沙人民再次生活的机会，让他们能够进口重建加沙所需的机械，而他们现在无法做到这一点。

sentences.en: — We're speaking right at the end of the year.
sentences.zh: 这种持续了18年的苦难，实在是太多了，太多了。

sentences.en: What is your wish for the new year?
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我对新年的希望。

sentences.en: — I would like the end of the Gaza siege, which has been going on for 18 years.
sentences.zh: 这不是一件小事，这是一件大事，但这是我的希望。

sentences.en: And I think that if the siege ends and people are able to visit Gaza, especially Israelis,
sentences.zh: 拉贾，感谢你抽出时间与我交谈，祝你节日快乐。

sentences.en: and see what has been done to Gaza, then it might create a big change and awaken the Israeli people to the crime that they've committed in Gaza.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: And that could be very hopeful.
sentences.zh: 这可能会带来很大的希望。

sentences.en: And also, it gives a chance for the Gazan people to live again and to be able to import the machinery they need to rebuild Gaza, which they are not able to do now.
sentences.zh: 此外，这也让加沙人民有机会重获新生，并能够进口重建加沙所需的机械设备，而这是他们目前无法做到的。

sentences.en: And the suffering that has been going on for 18 years, it's too much, too much.
sentences.zh: 持续了十八年的苦难，实在是太多了，太多了。

sentences.en: And so this is my hope for the new year.
sentences.zh: 这就是我对新年的期盼。

sentences.en: And it is not a small thing, it's a big thing, but it's my hope.
sentences.zh: 这并非小事，而是一件大事，但这就是我的希望。
